questions.prompt: Why do TypeScript interfaces NOT protect an API endpoint from malformed JSON at runtime?

options.text: TypeScript types are erased at compile time, so runtime payloads must still be validated

code.source:
const raw: unknown = await res.json();
if (!isOrder(raw)) throw new TypeError('Invalid order');

questions.prompt: What does this mapped type do?

options.text: Transforms every property of `T` to have type `boolean`

code.source: type Flags<T> = { [K in keyof T]: boolean };

questions.prompt: What does `infer R` inside `type Unwrap<T> = T extends Promise<infer R> ? R : T;` do?

options.text: Captures the resolved inner type `R` when `T` matches `Promise<...>`

code.source: type Unwrap<T> = T extends Promise<infer R> ? R : T;

questions.prompt: Why do conditional types like `type ToArr<T> = T extends any ? T[] : never;` distribute over unions?

options.text: When `T` is a naked type parameter, TypeScript applies the conditional to each union member individually

questions.prompt: Select all compiler flags that strengthen TypeScript's null and property safety beyond basic `strict: true`. (Select all that apply.)
What does `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` enforce on `interface Cfg { port?: number }`?

options.text: `port` may be omitted, but cannot be explicitly set to `undefined` unless `number | undefined` is written

questions.prompt: What is a common pitfall of the non-null assertion `!` (`user!.name`) in production code?

options.text: It silences the compiler without checking at runtime, risking a `TypeError` if `user` is actually `null`/`undefined`

questions.prompt: Why does TypeScript's excess property checking trigger on `fn({ a: 1, extra: 2 })` but NOT when passing a variable `const x = { a: 1, extra: 2 }; fn(x);`?

options.text: Fresh object literals are assumed to have no hidden consumers, whereas variables may satisfy a broader structural contract

questions.prompt: What does `isolatedModules: true` ensure when using Babel, esbuild, SWC, or Vite to transpile TypeScript?

options.text: Each `.ts` file can be transpiled independently without cross-file type information (e.g., requiring `export type` for re-exported types)

questions.prompt: Select all practices that help migrate a large JavaScript codebase to TypeScript safely. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Enable `allowJs` and `checkJs` or convert leaf/core modules incrementally
Enable `strict: true` for new/converted files early rather than accumulating `any`
Add JSDoc or `.d.ts` types at module boundaries

questions.prompt: What trade-off does `skipLibCheck: true` in `tsconfig.json` make?

options.text: Skips checking your own application `.ts` files
Skips type-checking `.d.ts` files in `node_modules` for faster builds, at the risk of missing conflicting third-party declarations

questions.prompt: Why is `readonly T[]` preferred over `T[]` for function parameters that should not mutate caller data?

options.text: It prevents accidental `.push()`/`.sort()` mutations inside the function and accepts both mutable and readonly arrays
It converts the array to a `Set`

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `tsconfig.json` project references (`"composite": true` and `"references"`)?

options.text: To split a monorepo into smaller compilation units with incremental `.tsbuildinfo` caching

Pre-Node module resolution; avoid in new projects

questions.prompt: What does `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` enforce?

options.text: Type-only imports/exports must explicitly use `import type` / `export type` so emit is predictable

questions.prompt: Why does `Object.keys(obj)` return `string[]` instead of `(keyof typeof obj)[]` in TypeScript?

options.text: Because structural subtyping allows `obj` to have extra properties at runtime beyond its static type

questions.prompt: What does this branded type pattern prevent?

options.text: Accidentally passing an `OrderId` where a `UserId` is expected even though both are strings at runtime

code.source:
type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: unique symbol };
type OrderId = string & { readonly __brand: unique symbol };

options.text: ESLint replaces `tsc` completely for type checking
Rules like `no-floating-promises` catch unawaited Promises that `tsc` alone ignores
Rules like `no-unsafe-assignment` flag `any` leaking into typed variables

questions.prompt: What happens when a `tsc` library build forgets `"declaration": true`?

options.text: The JS code fails to run
Consumers of the published package receive no `.d.ts` type definitions

questions.prompt: Why should library public APIs often declare explicit return types on exported functions?

options.text: TypeScript requires them on all functions
Explicit return types prevent accidental breaking type changes and speed up compiler inference across packages

questions.prompt: What does `isolatedDeclarations: true` enable in TypeScript 5.5+?

options.text: Generating `.d.ts` files in parallel without full cross-file type inference by requiring explicit annotations on exports

questions.prompt: What risk does `const x = arr[i]` pose when `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is `false`?

options.text: `x` is typed as `T` even if `i` is out of bounds, hiding potential `undefined` runtime crashes

questions.prompt: Why is `Record<string, unknown>` better than `object` or `{}` for typing an arbitrary JSON object?

options.text: `{}` in TypeScript actually matches almost any non-nullish value (including `42` and `'hi'`), whereas `Record<string, unknown>` requires an indexable object

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to type React or UI component event/callback props cleanly in TypeScript. (Select all that apply.)

Use discriminated unions for mutually exclusive prop states

questions.prompt: What does `export type * from './types';` do?

options.text: Re-exports only type declarations from `./types` with zero runtime output

questions.prompt: Why can `const enum` cause issues when publishing a library or using `isolatedModules`?

options.text: `const enum` requires cross-file inlining at compile time, which single-file transpilers and `.d.ts` consumers cannot always inline

questions.prompt: What does `NoInfer<T>` (TypeScript 5.4+) prevent in this generic function?

options.text: It stops `initial` from widening or polluting inference of `S`, forcing `S` to be inferred from `states`

code.source: declare function createFSM<S>(initial: NoInfer<S>, states: S[]): void;

questions.prompt: What is a common pitfall when using `Object.assign(target, source)` in TypeScript?

options.text: It mutates `target` in place and its return type may not reflect narrowed constraints if `target` is typed loosely

questions.prompt: What does `satisfies` + `as const` together achieve on a configuration object?

options.text: Validates the config against a schema type while keeping exact literal values and `readonly` immutability

questions.prompt: What does `erasableSyntaxOnly` (TypeScript 5.8+) enforce?

options.text: Disallows TS-only runtime constructs (`enum`, namespaces with values, parameter properties) so files work with type-stripping runners

questions.prompt: Why should `package.json` `exports` specify `"types"` before `"default"` or `"import"`?

options.text: TypeScript resolves conditions in order and needs `"types"` first to pick up `.d.ts` files

questions.prompt: What does `Pick` vs `Omit` behave differently on when applied to a union of interfaces `A | B`?

options.text: Neither distributes over unions by default, which can collapse union-specific fields unless wrapped in a distributive conditional type

questions.prompt: When is a type-level `never` check useful in a conditional type?

options.text: `tsconfig` `paths` is only for compile-time resolution unless a bundler/loader also maps them, whereas `#imports` works natively in Node.js
